valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 17 Nov 2026 (rechecked 21 Nov 2026: Damodaran's site still blocked; web search again found only the global table). (1) Business: one business in effect, cables and conductors (cables 81% of 2025/26 segment profit before finance and other income; PVC compound 10% and aluminium/copper rods and accessories 7% mostly feed the cable plants: Annual Report 2025/26, p. 183). So one sector beta. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-in from a web-search extract of his global table (January 2026): Electrical Equipment, 1,158 firms, levered 1.37, D/E 13.74%, unlevered 1.25, cash 7.08% of firm value, unlevered corrected for cash 1.34. (3) Net cash (Rs 10.4bn at 30 Sep 2026, about 14% of market value), so debt to equity 0 and no relevering, as for other net-cash companies on this site: 1.34. Weighting the cash pile at a beta of zero would give an equity beta of about 1.15 (1.34 × 62/73), so 1.34 is on the cautious side. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found (GuruFocus shows none; no vendor figure in search results). (5) Higher of 1.34 and (no local figure) = 1.34. (6) Within 0.3–2, but high for a CSE share: the global sector includes many technology-heavy equipment makers; ACL's profit does swing with copper (−49% in 2023/24). (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (17 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 1.34 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 22.0%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 18% / 16.5% / 15% of 11 Nov, as the analysis brief now requires the shared CAPM method.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): cost of equity 23.5% / 22.0% / 20.5%, cost of debt 7.11% (interest paid 0.128 ÷ average borrowings and leases, FY 2026; AWPLR-linked short-term loans, below the calculator's usual range), tax 30.8%, debt weight 4.1% (net debt Rs 3.0bn = borrowings 5.049 + leases 0.027 − cash 2.080 at 30 Sep 2026, against market cap Rs 70.3bn at Rs 97.80). Unit trusts and deposits are no longer netted off debt here; they are valued in the DCF's add-on instead.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 4% / 8% / 11%; supported 14.5% (reinvestment rate 68.8% × return on capital 21.1%, FY 2026). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2026 (Annual Report 2025/26 pp. 120–125, 182). The supported rate is flattered: Rs 4.34bn of the Rs 4.37bn reinvestment was stock and receivables built up as copper prices rose (price, not volume). Profit kept × ROE gives 15.3%.

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 4% then 4% / Base 8% then 5% / Bull 11% then 6%
valuationInputs.reason: Five years, then long-run, below the 12.24% bond and WACC; long-run reinvestment 33% / 31% / 30% of after-tax operating profit. Revenue grew 21% in FY 2026 and 22% in H1 FY2027, mostly copper prices and exports.

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: Trailing after-tax operating profit Rs 5.9bn over operating capital about Rs 31.8bn at Sep 2026 (total equity 46.39 − net cash 10.37 − investment property, associates and FVOCI shares 4.24) = 18.5%; the calculator's 34.7% uses owners' equity only and the March 2025 base.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 5.00bn / Base Rs 5.88bn / Bull Rs 5.88bn (calculated)
valuationInputs.reason: Trailing operating profit Rs 9.196bn (FY 2026 9.178 + H1 FY2027 4.514 − H1 FY2026 4.496) less the one-off Rs 0.700bn investment property gain (note 38, p. 182), × (1 − 30.8% FY 2026 tax rate). Bear × 0.85: about the FY 2025 level (operating profit 7.466 less 0.086 gain × (1 − 32.1%) = Rs 5.0bn), i.e. copper prices fall back.

valuationInputs.name: Cash after maintenance capex (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear Rs 5.00bn / Base Rs 5.88bn / Bull Rs 5.89bn (calculated)
valuationInputs.reason: After-tax operating profit + FY 2026 depreciation Rs 0.368bn − maintenance capex (calculator range 0.368 / 0.368 / 0.354): cash before interest and before growth spending. Not the calculator's FY 2026 operating-cash figure (Rs 1.16bn), which is after Rs 4.34bn of stock and receivables build that the DCF already charges as reinvestment (growth ÷ return on capital).

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Capex booked Rs 0.40bn vs depreciation Rs 0.37bn in FY 2026; no growth project named, no capital commitments.

valuationInputs.name: Investments and minorities (add-on)
valuationInputs.value: Rs 15.49 a share (bear, base and bull)
valuationInputs.reason: Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 4: unit trusts (FVTPL) 6.229 + short-term deposits 7.140 + non-current deposits 0.053 + investment property 2.529 + associates 0.853 + FVOCI shares 0.858 = Rs 17.662bn, less non-controlling interests at book Rs 6.526bn (Damodaran: subtract minority interests from firm value; book value used) = Rs 11.136bn ÷ 718.724mn shares. Replaces the hand-applied 86% owners' share of 17 Nov, which the code can't express.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Five-year average about 21%, including a 29% year (2022/23); 11% in 2023/24; 18.7% FY 2026.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Now the same in every method (DCF, P/B, P/E, residual income); 6% / 6.5% / 7% before. Below the 12.24% bond yield.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027 × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 4.61; H2 Rs 2.99 / 4.49 / 5.69 (last year 4.52). Base equals the Rs 9.13 run-rate. P/E justified at the cost of equity: payout (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g). Before: 7.00 × 6 / 9.00 × 8 / 10.50 × 10.

valuationInputs.name: Residual income start ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Start ROE = twelve-month profit to owners Rs 6.559bn over average owners' equity of Sep 2025 (33.943) and Sep 2026 (39.863), worked out by scripts/derived.py. Payout 8% held for all ten years (the code's CFA form; Rs 0.60 dividend ÷ Rs 9.13 EPS = 7%); the 17 Nov hand calculation raised the payout after year 5, which is why residual income is lower now.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Sum of the parts (whole-company DCF + investments − minorities), P/E, justified P/B, residual income
valuationInputs.reason: All four from scripts/valuation.py. The DCF starts from after-tax operating profit because copper stock swings yearly cash flow. Dividend model left out (payout about 7%).

openQuestions: Q3 results (to December 2026, due by mid-February): does the gross margin recover from 24% (26–28% a year earlier), and is second-half EPS on track for the base case's Rs 4.49 (Rs 4.52 a year earlier)?
Does inventory (Rs 19.1bn at Sep 2026, Rs 14.1bn in March) start to fall and release cash, and are the Rs 4.4bn of short-term loans and Rs 0.5bn overdraft repaid?
Unit trusts fell to Rs 6.2bn from Rs 8.7bn as they were cashed to fund stock: does the investment pile keep shrinking?
Exchange gains and losses: Rs 590mn gain in Q1, Rs 144mn loss in Q2; how big is the swing next quarter?
Beta: in January 2027 replace the global Electrical Equipment stand-in (1.34) with Damodaran's emerging-markets figure, and look for three local 5-year betas.
Shareholding: the Madanayake family's 62.08% is now all in Mr H.A.S. (Suren) Madanayake's name (U.G. and N.C. Madanayake held 38.15% and 1.72% in March). Check the annual report for the reason.
Interim cash flow shows interest net (received less paid) inside operating cash: record interest paid if the next interim splits it out, so the twelve-month cash before interest can be worked out.

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/redo ACL.N0000 full). Rebuilt the record and analysis from the CSE copies of the 2025/26 annual report and the September 2026 interim. Added the reinvestment figures for FY 2025 and FY 2026 (capex booked 0.31 / 0.40, depreciation 0.36 / 0.37, working capital build 1.50 / 4.34, operating profit 7.47 / 9.18 incl. a 0.70bn investment property gain, tax 32.1% / 30.8%, interest paid in operating cash 0.27 / 0.13, borrowings 1.39 / 2.18, net cash 12.5 / 14.8, minorities), a Q2 FY2027 quarter and a 12-month EPS of Rs 9.13. Corrected the cash flow page reference (p. 125, not p. 124). No restatements found. Applied the current brief: beta 1.34 (provisional, Damodaran global Electrical Equipment via web search; his site and local 5-year betas unavailable), cost of equity = WACC 22.0% (16.5% before), whole-company DCF added, P/E multiples now justified at the cost of equity, long-term growth 4/5/6% in every method, growth check and run-rate checks pass. Fair value Rs 64.70 → 39.10, buy Rs 55.00 → 33.20, strong buy Rs 48.50 → 29.30; price Rs 101.00 (CSE close 17 Nov 2026). Business tests 3 of 4 (fails cash), category 2 watch list, unchanged. The fall is driven by the required return; at a cash-weighted beta of 1.15 fair value would be about Rs 44.50.

changeLog.basedOn: Annual Report 2025/26 and interim to 30 Sep 2026 (CSE copies, re-read in full)
changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/redo ACL.N0000 APLA.N0000 full). Rebuilt the research record in the current 'report figures only' format: printed lines with pages, the interim's comparative columns (H1 FY2026, Q2 FY2026) as their own periods, no worked-out ratios, net debt, tax rates or twelve-month figures (scripts/derived.py now works those out). Added management (plans and promises vs delivery), shareholders (top 20 at Sep 2026 vs March 2026) and code-computed modelInputs. The DCF is now a sum of the parts (DCF of the operating business, plus unit trusts, deposits, investment property, associates and FVOCI shares, less minorities at book) instead of a hand-applied 86% owners' share; net debt for WACC is now borrowings + leases − cash (Rs 3.0bn), so WACC is 21.3% (22.0% before). Residual income is lower (Rs 29.13 against Rs 34.13) because the code holds the 8% payout for all ten years, where the 17 Nov hand calculation raised it after year 5. Price Rs 97.80 (CSE close 20 Nov 2026). Category unchanged: watch list (3 of 4 tests).
